prototype_feel_reasons: The first hotspot label overlaps the left character’s face/head and map-reading activity in both viewports.
The mobile crop removes the right-side worker almost entirely, weakening the intended three-job overview before interaction.
Hotspot markers are placed over character hands and work objects instead of adjacent negative space.
Overlay sizing and placement feel mechanically anchored rather than composed around the illustrated subjects.
issues: library scene/first hotspot label — label covers the left worker’s face/head and part of the map needed to understand the job — move the label into nearby shelf space or below the table edge and connect it with a short pointer.

library scene/center translucent hotspot — marker sits directly over the conservator’s hand and focal work surface — offset it beside the object or reduce its size while preserving the tap target invisibly.

library scene/mobile viewport — horizontal crop hides the entire right-side worker and cuts the scanner station at the edge — use a slightly wider mobile framing, reduce scene scale, or set an initial object-position that previews all three subjects.

library scene/mobile carousel — important content reaches the container edge without a strong visual continuation cue inside the artwork — add a subtle edge fade or visible sliver of the next subject while keeping the rounded mask.

library scene/overlay hierarchy — large opaque speech label dominates the characters and competes with the scene — shorten the label, reduce its footprint, and reserve opaque overlays for areas without faces, hands, or tools.
BADGE_COLLISION: overlay covers a subject's face/head/tools
